text: Time to put this entire chapter together in one real scenario. The task: write a Script Include method that finds every open, unassigned Priority 1 incident older than 24 hours, reassigns each one to a fallback group, and returns a count — written efficiently, avoiding every pitfall from the last lesson.

Open means active is true. Unassigned means assigned_to is empty. Older than 24 hours means sys_created_on is before a cutoff computed with gs.hoursAgo of 24. The method takes the fallback group's sys_id as its one parameter, and needs to return how many incidents it actually reassigned.

The query combines four conditions with addQuery and addNullQuery, all ANDed together — active, priority 1, assigned_to is null, and created before the cutoff — and query is called exactly once. That cutoff timestamp is computed a single time, outside the loop, not recalculated per row.

Inside the while-next loop, each pass is already positioned on one matching incident, so setValue and dot notation set the assignment group and work notes directly, update saves that row immediately, and reassignedCount increments once per row actually processed. The return value is exactly the number of incidents this call touched.

Walk through why each Lesson 16 pitfall is avoided here. There's no N+1, because exactly one GlideRecord and one query call exist — the loop updates rows it already found, it never opens a second GlideRecord per row. There's no wasted getRowCount, because the loop's own counter produces the total for free. There's no setLimit here, because the job is to act on every matching incident, not a sample. And GlideAggregate isn't used, because this method has to modify rows, and GlideAggregate can only compute read-only totals, never update anything.

One combined query, one efficient loop, one honest count — that's GlideRecord done right. This closes out the GlideRecord chapter. Next, Chapter Four: why client scripts need a bridge to the server, and the GlideAjax pattern that provides it.
